newsitem.title: USA: Duke Power to buy PanEnergy for $7.7 billion in stock.
newsitem.headline: Duke Power to buy PanEnergy for $7.7 billion in stock.

text.p: Duke Power Co. said Monday that it will acquire natural gas pipeline operator PanEnergy Corp. for about $7.7 billion in a tax-free stock transaction that merges two of the biggest companies in their respective industries.
The deal will combine one of the largest and lowest-cost electric utilities in the country with North America's third largest marketer of natural gas.

Duke is an electric utility in Charlotte, N.C., serving 1.8 million customers, while PanEnergy, a Houston-based energy services company, operates one of the biggest interstate natural gas pipeline networks, handling more than 15 percent of the natural gas consumed in the United States.

"This strategic merger is about growth, opportunity and creating value," Duke Chairman William H. Grigg said in a statement. "Each of our companies has a recognised name and a strong reputation in our industries. This combination creates the preeminent provider of energy and energy services in North America.

"Both Duke Power and PanEnergy realise that the convergence of the gas and electricity industries means that a combined company would achieve distinct advantages not available to either on a stand-alone basis," Grigg added.
Under the definitive merger agreement, Duke is to offer 1.0444 shares of its stock for each share of PanEnergy in a tax-free polling of interests.
After the merger, PanEnergy stockholders will own about 44 percent of the common stock of the new company, which will be called Duke Energy Corp.

Based on Duke's closing price of $47.875 on Friday, PanEnergy stockholders will receive about $50 a share for each PanEnergy share they hold. PanEnergy's stock closed Friday at $42.25 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.
Upon completion of the merger, Richard Priory, currently president and chief operating officer of Duke Power, will become chairman and chief executive of Duke Energy.
Paul Anderson, president and CEO of PanEnergy, will become president and chief operating officer of the new company.

Grigg will retire as chairman and chief executive of Duke Power and Dennis Hendrix will step down as chairman of PanEnergy and join Duke Energy's board, which will have 11 members from Duke Power and seven from PanEnergy.

"As the gas and electric markets have begun to converge, we have recognised a need to align ourselves with an electric partner," PanEnergy's Anderson said. "Duke Power is the acknowledged industry leader in providing safe, reliable, responsive and economical service to its customers. It is upon this bedrock that we will build a true industry pacesetter in the field of energy services."
Duke said it anticipates that the transaction will add to earnings at the end of the second year after its completion.

Duke, which currently pays an annual dividend of $2.12 per share, said PanEnergy shareholders will receive an increase of $1.25 in dividends per share, based on the implied exchange ratio, from PanEnergy's current dividend of 96 cents a share.
After completion of the merger, PanEnergy will be a wholly-owned subsidiary of Duke Energy, which will be headquartered in Charlotte, N.C.
Under the merger agreement, there are no changes required with respect to either company's public debt issues or the outstanding preferred stock of Duke Power.
The merger is conditioned upon the approval of the stockholders of both companies and the completion of government regulatory procedures.
Duke said it expects the regulatory procedures can be completed in less than 12 months.
